title: Webb finds most distant known galaxy (JADES-GS-z14-0 environment NIRCam image)
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, J. Olmsted (STScI), S. Carniani (Scuola Normale Superiore), JADES Collaboration

geometryEvidence.reference: A picture of the sky, centred on the object, so its plane faces the Sun. The recipe's inclination of 0.001° is not a measurement: the bake needs a plane with some depth along the sight line, and this is the smallest tilt that gives it one.

registration.method: The file's embedded tags give 0.02991 arcsec per pixel and north 38.0° right of vertical. They place the paper's position 1.5 arcsec from the galaxy the publisher marks in its annotated version (ESA/Webb jades4), so the window is centred on that marked galaxy instead: its orange light and the pale galaxy beside it, as the publisher's enlarged view shows them. The window's centre is taken to be the paper's position, to about 0.1 arcsec.

displayModel: The picture lies on one flat plane facing the Sun at the object's comoving distance. Nothing in the picture has depth: seen from the side it is a line.
coverage: An 80 px window (2.4 arcsec) of the publisher's Large JPEG, not resampled. The pale galaxy beside the orange one is a foreground galaxy.

acquisition.operation: packages/bake/authoring/far-destinations/picture-source.mts: download the publisher's Large JPEG, cut the window without resampling; JPEG quality 95.
